feedback: Pre-race review, based only on earlier races and the candidate's contents. The candidate is valid: five sensors match five weights, x-positions are within ±0.08 m, and ki = 0.5 is inside its 0–5 range with the integral capped at ±2. It changes one group from the best raced design (iteration 3, score 40.69): controller.ki from 0.3 to 0.5, with geometry, kp 2.5, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4 and line_loss last_direction unchanged. Iteration 3 showed line_loss_events 0 on all three tracks and max_error still at 0.0609 to 0.0629 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Its s-bend and slalom oscillation was low (0.0665 and 0.0633) with progress of only 0.041 and 0.035, which points to steady drift rather than jitter, so a larger integral term is the change the evidence supports. The oval oscillation (0.113) was not moved by kp in iteration 3, so it is not a proportional-gain problem, and this candidate does not address it. The rationale's expected outcomes are hypotheses only and are not measured. Use the next race as follows. (a) If the s-bend or slalom progress falls, or max_error rises above 0.0629, the integral is overcorrecting: return ki to 0.3. (b) If line_loss_events stays 0 and max_error on the s-bend and slalom drops below 0.06 with progress near 1 and completion_time above 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.7. (c) If oval steering_oscillation stays above about 0.09, test kd at 0.2 before lowering kp again. Change one group of fields per revision.
requested_changes: If the s-bend or slalom progress falls below iteration 3's 0.041 and 0.035, or max_error rises above 0.0629, revert controller.ki to 0.3 and keep kp at 2.5, since iteration 3 is the best raced design.
If line_loss_events stays 0 and max_error drops below 0.06 with progress near 1 and completion_time above 3 s, set controller.base_speed to 1.7 and keep the other fields.
If oval steering_oscillation stays above about 0.09 (iteration 3 measured 0.113), set controller.kd from 0.1 to 0.2 with ki and kp unchanged before lowering kp again.
